findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without acquiring cacheMu, while BuildIndex now inserts into that map under only a brief lock at the end of a potentially long build. Concurrent index creation (startup initialization with multiple workers, or lazy getOrCreateIndex during Search) can therefore race with TotalDocs, causing a data race and potentially a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic. TotalDocs should hold cacheMu.RLock while iterating, or snapshot the indexes first.

findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key are no longer serialized
findings.body: Removing the whole-function cacheMu lock means two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource can both create a bleve index, run the builder, and then overwrite b.cache[key]. For file-backed indexes both calls use the same directory, so the second bleve.New can fail or conflict with the first; for memory indexes the overwritten index is leaked without being closed and in-flight searches may keep using a different instance than the cached one. The finer-grained locking needs a per-key build lock/singleflight, and any replaced index should be closed.

findings.title: searchSupport.init mutates shared counters and err from errgroup goroutines
findings.body: Inside group.Go, totalBatchesIndexed++ and '_, _, err = s.build(...)' mutate variables declared outside the goroutine. With initWorkers > 1 these run concurrently, so the counter increment is racy/lost and the shared err can be overwritten by a succeeding build after a failing one (or vice versa), meaning group.Wait may not reliably report the failing build and the span attribute may be wrong. Use an atomic counter and a local '_, _, err := s.build(...); return err' inside each goroutine.

findings.title: Failed eager Init leaks the server background context and any started watch goroutine
findings.body: NewResourceServer now calls s.Init(ctx) during construction and, on error, returns nil without calling s.cancel(). If search.init succeeded far enough to start its watch goroutine (which uses context.Background in searchSupport.init) or lifecycle/watcher setup partially started, those goroutines and the claims context created at line 229 are never cancelled because the caller never receives the server to Stop. Construction failure should cancel s.cancel() (and stop any partially started lifecycle/search watcher) before returning the error.
